questions.text: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct about HTTP cookies?
questions.solution:
A cookie is a small piece of data (name-value text) stored by the browser, not executable code.

It does come in the Set-Cookie HTTP header, has an expiry time and can track browsing on a site.

Answer: A cookie is a piece of code that has the potential to compromise security

options: A cookie is a piece of code that has the potential to compromise the security of an Internet user
A cookie gains entry to the user's work area through an HTTP header
A cookie has an expiry date and time
Cookies can be used to track the browsing pattern of a user at a particular site

questions.text: A link has a transmission speed of [latex]10^{6}[/latex] bits/sec. It uses data packets of size 1000 bytes each. Assume that the acknowledgment has negligible transmission delay, and that its propagation delay is the same as the data propagation delay. Also assume that the processing delays at nodes are negligible. The efficiency of the stop-and-wait protocol in this setup is exactly 25%. The value of the one-way propagation delay (in milliseconds) is ________.
questions.solution:
[latex]T_t=\frac{8000}{10^6}=8[/latex] ms.

[latex]\eta=\frac{T_t}{T_t+2T_p}=0.25\Rightarrow 8+2T_p=32\Rightarrow T_p=12[/latex] ms

Answer: 12

questions.text: Consider a LAN with four nodes [latex]S_{1},S_{2},S_{3} \; and \; S_{4}[/latex] . Time is divided into fixed-size slots, and a node can begin its transmission only at the beginning of a slot. A collision is said to have occurred if more than one node transmit in the same slot. The probabilities of generation of a frame in a time slot by [latex]S_{1},S_{2},S_{3} \; and \;  S_{4}[/latex] are 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 and 0.4, respectively. The probability of sending a frame in the first slot without any collision by any of these four stations is _____________.
questions.solution:
Success = exactly one station transmits.

- Only S1: 0.1 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.8 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.7 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.6 = 0.0336
- Only S2: 0.9 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.2 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.7 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.6 = 0.0756
- Only S3: 0.9 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.8 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.3 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.6 = 0.1296
- Only S4: 0.9 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.8 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.7 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.4 = 0.2016

Total = 0.4404

Answer: 0.44

questions.text: Suppose that the stop-and-wait protocol is used on a link with a bit rate of 64 kilobits per second and 20 milliseconds propagation delay. Assume that the transmission time for the acknowledgement and the processing time at nodes are negligible. Then the minimum frame size in bytes to achieve a link utilization of at least 50% is______________.
questions.solution:
Stop-and-wait utilization = [latex]\frac{T_t}{T_t+2T_p}\ge\frac12\Rightarrow T_t\ge2T_p=40[/latex] ms.

Frame size = [latex]64\times10^3\times40\times10^{-3}=2560[/latex] bits = 320 bytes.

Answer: 320

questions.text: In one of the pairs of protocols given below, both the protocols can use multiple TCP connections between the same client and the server. Which one is that?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- HTTP: a browser can open several parallel TCP connections to the same server.
- FTP: uses a control connection plus separate data connections.

TELNET and SMTP use a single connection.

Answer: HTTP, FTP
